checks.issue: THE PAGE OPENS MID-ITEM. Verses 25-28 finish item 2, whose numeral is on page 312, so no verse on this sheet carries para_start until verse 29. The chant's layout is 'lines' and the group agrees with it, so no para_layout is needed either — declaring one here would be noise.

THE SHEET IS SKEWED AND THE GAP RULE FAILS ON IT. The left edge drifts from x 399 at the head to x 356 at the foot, and the vertical gaps compress with it: item 3 breaks at 71px, item 4 at 70px, item 5 at only 54px. Read by gap alone, item 5 would have been folded into item 4. The NUMERALS hang left of the text — x 317, 310 and 300 against a text indent of x 390 falling to x 356 — and that is what settles the grouping on this page.

THE BOOK SPELLS THE SAME WORD TWO WAYS ON ONE SHEET. Verse 39 prints 'viññāna' with a plain n where verse 33 prints 'viññāṇakhandho' with the retroflex. Both read clearly at 5x. Kept as each line sets it, NOT made to agree.

The book prints 'aniccalakkhaṇapārami' with a SHORT final i, where the standard form is pāramī. It is printed the same way on all five lines of item 3, so it is the book's reading rather than one slip. Recorded as printed.

Verse 28 is a bare 'itipi so bhagavā.' closing item 2 — the shortest line in the chant, and it is the line whose gap profile proved the word spacing: 14 gaps, median 5px, with the top two at 10 and 9px, matching exactly the two word spaces it contains.

batch_status.paiboon_scan: clean, and trivially so. The page prints no Thai, so every paiboon is empty and there is no Paiboon+ anywhere in the batch. Scanned every romanised slot for kh, th, ph and ng standing in for Thai consonants: zero hits — the kh in khandho and the th in paṭhavī are the page's own IAST.
batch_status.pali_untouched: Confirmed, with the sense inverted for this section. There is no Thai-script pali to leave untouched — every pali value is empty by design — and every pali_roman is the page's own roman text copied letter for letter INCLUDING ITS SPACING: dotted m, n with dot below in saraṇaṃ and viññāṇakhandho, l with dot below in cakkavāḷa, t with dot below in paṭhavī, long ī in nimmānaratī and paranimmitavasavattī. The two places the book disagrees with itself — viññāna against viññāṇa, and the short i in pārami — are recorded in checks rather than quietly fixed.
batch_status.page_scan: agrees. One row for one page covering verses 25-50, the whole of what this page adds. Verse 25 carries the page key and deliberately carries nothing else, because the item it belongs to opened on page 312. No verse is orphaned and none is claimed twice. No page blocks and no footnotes on this sheet.
batch_status.notes: Two findings. (1) A SKEWED SHEET DEFEATS THE VERTICAL-GAP RULE. The photograph's left edge drifts 43px across the page and the paragraph gaps compress with it, so item 5's break measures 54px against item 3's 71px — below the threshold that has grouped every previous page. The hanging numerals are what settle it. Any page photographed at an angle needs the same care. (2) THE WORD SPACING IS NARROW AND WAS SETTLED ON PAGE 312 by measuring gaps against each line's own median rather than an absolute width; this sheet is transcribed with ordinary word division on that basis, and verse 28 is the cleanest single piece of evidence for it.
